Worth a read: https://www.postgresql.org/about/news/
The new async I/O in Postgres 18 could cut our booking-history report from ~4s to well under 1s, since it's mostly sequential scans. I'd like to benchmark it on staging next sprint before we decide anything.

messages.author: Ben Ortiz
messages.text: Quick question: why does the booking form submit twice on slow networks? I added a loading state but it still happens sometimes 😅

replies.author: Maya Chen
replies.text:
Good question. The loading state only disables the button after React re-renders, so a fast double tap gets two submits in before that. Two fixes:
1. Guard in the handler with a ref (isSubmitting.current) so the second call returns immediately.
2. Send an idempotency key with the request, so the API ignores a duplicate even if one slips through.
We already support idempotency keys in /bookings, you just need to pass the header.

replies.author: Ben Ortiz
replies.text: That worked, thank you! Added both.

replies.author: Maya Chen
replies.text: Nice. Can you add a test that fires two submits in a row? That way it can't come back quietly.

messages.author: Maya Chen
messages.text: Heads up: checkout p95 latency jumped from 300ms to 2.4s after this afternoon's deploy. Looking into it now.

replies.author: Maya Chen
replies.text: Found it. The new promo banner loads each user's coupons one booking at a time, so checkout does 40+ queries instead of 1 (N+1). Rolling the banner back behind its feature flag now.

replies.author: Leo Tan
replies.text: I'm around, want me to write the batched query?

replies.author: Maya Chen
replies.text: Yes please. Flag is off and p95 is back to 310ms. Let's ship the batched version tomorrow with a query-count test so this gets caught in CI next time.

replies.author: Leo Tan
replies.text: Batched query is up for review. Checkout now runs 2 queries regardless of basket size, and the new test fails if it goes above 3.

replies.author: Maya Chen
replies.text: Reviewed and merged. I'll write a short incident note for the team so everyone knows what to look for.

messages.author: Maya Chen
messages.text:
Incident note: checkout slowdown, 3 Oct.
What happened: an N+1 query in the promo banner took p95 from 300ms to 2.4s for ~25 minutes.
What we changed: batched query (thanks Leo) plus a CI test that fails when checkout runs more than 3 queries.
Tip for reviews: any loop that calls the API or the DB inside a render path is worth a second look.

messages.author: Ben Ortiz
messages.text:
Found this while fixing the date picker: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Temporal
Temporal handles time zones properly, which is exactly what keeps breaking our booking times for users abroad. Polyfill is small. Could we try it in the date picker first?

messages.author: Leo Tan
messages.text:
Proposal for the payments retry logic before launch:
Option A: retry in the API request (simple, but the user waits up to 10s).
Option B: queue the retry and email the receipt when it succeeds (more moving parts, but checkout stays fast).
I lean towards B, since it matches how notifications already work and Ravi's queue fix makes it reliable. Thoughts by Friday?

replies.author: Ravi Kumar
replies.text: B works for me, the queue can take it now.

replies.author: Nora Ahmad
replies.text: B from the product side too, as long as the receipt email says the payment is processing.

replies.author: Leo Tan
replies.text: Going with B. Implemented, with the processing message Nora asked for, and added it to the rollback doc.
